summary: I like that the entire memory layer is a git repo of Markdown with `[[wikilinks]]` and a `[source: …]` tag on every entry, so you can grep it, diff it, and audit provenance without spinning up a vector database, which is the kind of inspectable, local-first design I actually trust. The Dreaming loop, a periodic agent that merges duplicates and resolves contradictions, is a small but sharp way to keep that repo from rotting, and the composability model where parallel sessions push to the same repo and let git flag conflicts maps directly onto what PenguPool needs when I fan work out across sessions. It ships as a spec rather than a product, which I appreciate; it gives me a format to fold into my own agent tooling without locking into anyone's cloud.
